title: Refactoring the Book Store
idea: A refactor moves code without changing what it does. The Book Store splits into model, controller (the handlers), routes and app files.
points: Move one layer at a time, then re-run the same requests.
A router, made with `express.Router()`, holds routes; `app.use('/books', router)` mounts it.
Mounted routes drop the prefix: `router.get('/:id')` answers `GET /books/:id`.
`app.js` builds and exports the app; `server.js` imports it and calls `listen`.

code.title: The controller
code.caption: A controller is a module of handler functions. These are part 2's handlers, now calling the model. Save as `src/controllers/books.controller.js`.

walk.text: The controller reaches the data only through the model's exported functions.
Helpers moved from part 2: the body check and the JSON error replies.
The read handlers ask the model; `getBook` answers `404` when it returns `undefined`.
`createBook` checks the body, asks the model to store it, and replies `201`.
`updateBook` keeps part 2's order: missing book first, then bad body, then the change.
`deleteBook` replies `204` if the model removed a book, `404` otherwise.

code.title: The routes
code.caption: Only the map from method and path to handler stays here. Save as `src/routes/books.routes.js`.

walk.text: Import `Router` and every controller function as one namespace.
Paths are relative to the mount point: `/` here means `/books`.
`app.js` imports this router and mounts it with `app.use('/books', booksRouter)`.

code.title: Same requests, new layout
code.caption: Run from the project root. These are part 2's requests; compare the output, because only the layout changed.

walk.text: `src/app.js` builds the app, adds `express.json()`, mounts the router, and exports it.
Importing starts nothing. This script calls `listen(0)` to use any free port.
`call` sends one JSON request and prints the method, path, status and body.
Part 2's six requests: create, fix with `PUT`, two failures, then `DELETE` twice.
A final `GET /books` confirms which ids survived.
Close the server so the script can exit.

pitfalls: Do not add features while moving code: you cannot tell what broke.
Fix import paths after every move: `../` climbs one folder, `./` stays put.
Do not call `listen` in `app.js`: every import would start a server.

quiz.why: The router is mounted at `/books`, so `/books/7` matches `/:id`. A bare `/7` is outside the mount, so Express answers 404.

takeaway: Each file does one job; `app.js` only wires them together.

starters: Why export the app instead of calling `listen` in `app.js`?
Can one router be mounted at two different paths?
How do I know a refactor did not break anything?
